bib.title: Failing Loudly: An Empirical Study of Methods for Detecting Dataset Shift

read.skipped: Appendix (pp14-38) is plots only; read captions and labels, not curves.

question: Which combination of dimensionality reduction and two-sample test best detects dataset shift in high-dimensional data from few samples, and can the shift be characterised and judged harmful or benign?
hypothesis: A pipeline of black-box dimensionality reduction followed by two-sample testing detects shift well, with BBSD-style label-classifier outputs working even when label shift assumptions fail.
contributions: Empirical comparison of dimensionality reduction (NoRed, PCA, SRP, UAE, TAE, BBSDs, BBSDh, domain classifier) with MMD, KS+Bonferroni, chi-squared and binomial tests
Domain classifier used to surface most anomalous samples and a heuristic to judge shift malignancy
Finding that the original MNIST split shows a (harmless) shift

method.summary: Source and target samples are reduced to low-dimensional representations, then compared with two-sample tests (MMD, per-dimension KS with Bonferroni, chi-squared for hard labels, binomial for domain-classifier accuracy). Shifts are simulated on MNIST and CIFAR-10 test sets and detection accuracy is measured at 8 target sample sizes.

datasets.name: MNIST
datasets.split: random split; shift applied to test set only

datasets.name: Fashion MNIST, SVHN, original splits
datasets.source: Xiao et al. 2017; Netzer et al. 2011

models.name: Autoencoder (UAE untrained, TAE trained)
models.architecture: convolutional, 3 conv layers and 1 fully connected layer

models.name: Label classifier (BBSDs, BBSDh) and domain classifier (Classif)

training.objective: autoencoder reconstruction loss; classification for label/domain classifiers
training.seeds: 5 random splits; DR training data kept constant, val/test split varies

inference.samples: test sample sizes s in {10,20,50,100,200,500,1000,10000}; kernel methods only up to 1000; 5 random splits

parameters.K: 32 for PCA, SRP, UAE, TAE; C for BBSDs; 1 for BBSDh and Classif
parameters.MMD kernel: squared exponential, sigma = median distance in aggregate sample; p-value by permutation test
parameters.domain_classifier_split: source and target each halved; first half trains, second half tested with binomial test vs 0.5

metrics.name: detection accuracy
metrics.definition: not formally defined; inferred: share of runs in which the test rejects H0 at alpha=0.05

eval.protocol: Shift types: adversarial FGSM, knock-out class 0, Gaussian noise, image transforms, image+knock-out, only-zero+image, original splits, domain-adaptation datasets; no-shift case included for false positives; mean over 5 random splits.

limits: Mostly image classification; NLP and graphs left to future work.
Online detection left open: adjacent time steps are correlated.
Dimensionality reduction is surjective so pathological shifts can be missed; authors speculate unlikely in non-adversarial settings.
Detection accuracy is not formally defined; pooled across datasets and shift strengths with only 5 splits; no variance in tables.
Malignancy heuristic needs an external labelling function, which the authors call a strong assumption; goals (ii) and (iii) are preliminary.
Shifts touching 10% of data are hard to detect; authors suggest outlier detection.

terms.definition: black box shift detection: use outputs of an off-the-shelf label classifier as the reduced representation (BBSDs softmax, BBSDh hard labels)
